transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, my regular doctor told me I needed to come see you. He says I've gotten too thin. I mean, I can see that my work pants are hanging pretty loose on me lately, but... to be honest, part of me still feels relieved when the number on the scale is lower. So, he wanted me to talk to someone about it.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yes, I am. I mean, if I eat something a bit heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I... I spend the rest of the day just scared that it's going to show on me. I end up keeping on checking myself, just thinking about how I need to make up for it somehow.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you can't stop?

No, I... no, I don't do that. I never eat a large amount of food all at once. If anything, it's the exact opposite for me. I usually stick to very small amounts. I definitely don't ever get that feeling where I can't stop eating.
Do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain after eating?

No, I don't really do anything like that. I just... I mostly just try to avoid eating too much in the first place. I don't make myself sick or take any pills or anything, if that's what you mean. I just stick to my routine and try to keep moving while I'm working.
Do you think your weight is a problem even when others say you are too thin?

Yes, I do. People might say I'm too thin, but I just don't see it like that. For me... when I stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right. It feels manageable. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit full, I just feel like I've completely let myself go. So, what other people say doesn't really change how I see it.
How much weight have you lost recently?

I'm not exactly sure of the exact number of pounds, but... my doctor recently told me I've gotten too thin. I know my work pants are definitely hanging loose on me now when I'm cleaning. But, honestly, part of me still feels relieved when I step on the scale and see that the number is lower.
Do you think your body shape or weight is normal when you look in the mirror?

Well, kind of like I was saying a minute ago... I don't know if I'd use the word normal, but it's what looks right to me. 

When I look in the mirror and see that I'm small and neat, it just tells me I'm handling everything right. But if I look and my stomach seems even the least bit full, it just looks wrong to me. I instantly feel like I've completely let myself go. So, I guess my version of normal is just... staying as small as I can.
Can you describe what happens when you do eat more than you usually do?

Well... if I eat something heavier, like some biscuits or pasta, it just really bothers me. I spend the rest of the day scared that it's going to show on me right away. I end up just... keeping on checking myself in the mirror or looking down at my stomach, and I can't stop thinking that I need to make up for it somehow.
Have you experienced any changes in your menstrual cycle?
No, not at all. I mean, I'm 64, so I went through menopause quite a few years ago. I haven't had a cycle in a long time, so... there haven't been any changes with that.
Do you think you would still be afraid of gaining weight if you couldn't see yourself in the mirror or measure your weight?

I... I don't really know for sure. I guess I'd still be afraid, yes. Even if I couldn't see it or measure it, I think I'd still feel it, you know? Like, I'd still feel heavy or full, and that feeling alone is enough to scare me. The mirror and the scale just... confirm what I'm already worrying about. But the fear is always there, no matter what.
Is there a specific weight or body shape that you think would be ideal for you?

I don't really have an exact number on the scale in mind. It's more about... well, my shape. When I stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right. Like I'm keeping things in order. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit full, I just feel like I've completely let myself go. So I guess my ideal is just staying small enough that I don't have to feel that way.
Do you think there is a specific weight or size that you are trying to maintain to avoid feeling fat?

I don't really have a specific number or size I'm aiming for. Like I was just saying, it's not about the scale for me. It's just... I just want to stay small enough so I don't feel heavy or out of control. There's no exact target, just... as long as I don't feel that fullness.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is because of how you think you look or because of something else?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean, how I look is definitely part of it, like I said about my stomach. But... I don't know if it's *just* about how I look. It's more about that feeling of being in control, I guess. Like, if I gain weight, it means I've failed at keeping myself in check. So maybe it's a bit of both.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is related to how you perceive your body shape or size?

I guess it is, yeah. Like I mentioned before, if my stomach looks round or full, I just feel terrible. So I do look at my shape, and if it seems bigger, I get really anxious about gaining weight. It's just hard to separate the two.
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about how you think your body would look if you gained weight?

I think it is, mostly. Like I was just saying, they kind of go hand in hand for me. When I stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right in my life. But... if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit full, I just feel like I've completely let myself go. So yeah, seeing that happen to my body is what really scares me.
